panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Patient MRI panel demonstrating enhancing synovial inflammation and edema around the third right MCP joint in a case specifically attributed to disseminated gonococcal infection presenting as isolated septic arthritis. [raw subtype: gonococcal arthritis] B: Patient MRI showing synovial hyperenhancement at the right third MCP joint, consistent with the septic arthritis attributed to disseminated gonococcal infection. [raw subtype: gonococcal arthritis] C: Patient post-contrast MRI demonstrating effusion and surrounding inflammatory change at the third right MCP joint in the reported disseminated gonococcal infection. [raw subtype: gonococcal arthritis]

panels.figure_caption: MRI of the right hand showing T1-weighted sagittal (A), proton density with contrast (B), and T1-weighted post-contrast (C) views showing synovial enhancement, effusion, and periarticular edema surrounding the third right MCP joint. (A) Joint capsule hyperenhancement is indicated by the white arrow, and subcutaneous hyperenhancement is indicated by the red arrow. (B) Synovial hyperenhancement is highlighted by the white arrow. (C) Effusion is shown by the white arrow. MRI: magnetic resonance imaging; MCP: metacarpophalangeal
in_text_mentions: DNA, and a respiratory viral panel were negative. A bilateral hand X-ray revealed no acute osseous abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the right hand revealed a large third MCP joint effusion with synovial enhancement and marked surrounding periarticular edema, concerning for septic arthritis (Figure 2). Orthopedic surgery was consulted and recommended one dose of intravenous (IV) vancomycin for empiric coverage of the septic joint and took the patient to the operating room on the day of admission for arthrotomy with debridement and irrigation (D&I) of the right third MCP joint.
